A.depoimento: I am sending my entire army to capture the neutral village of Santarem. While they march, I am building an archer at my capital, Lisboa, to secure my homeland.
A.plano: Capture Santarem to expand my territory. I have sent all my current troops to attack the neutral knight there. Meanwhile, I am building an archer at Lisboa to have some defense while the army is away. Next turn, I will check the battle outcome and plan the next expansion towards Coimbra or Badajoz.

B.depoimento: Our armies have marched to secure Tarragona and Girona. With our forces acting in unison, these neutral settlements will soon fly our colors, bringing prosperity and strength to our kingdom.
B.plano: Send 3 spearman and 1 archer to Tarragona, and 2 spearman, 3 archer, and 2 knights to Girona to capture both neutral villages. Build 1 archer in Barcelona to reinforce the capital next turn. Keep 1 knight in Barcelona for defense.

A.depoimento: I have ordered my main army from Santarem to march on Coimbra, hoping to secure another village and expand my territory. The archer in Lisboa is sent to Santarem to join the main force, and I am building more archers in the capital to prepare for future campaigns.
A.plano: I am focusing on expanding south and west where neutral villages are weak. I will attack Coimbra with my main army from Santarem. I will send the archer from Lisboa to Santarem to reinforce it. I am building two archers in Lisboa to increase my troop production. Next turn, I will check the battle outcome at Coimbra and decide whether to push towards Porto or Badajoz.

B.depoimento: Our scouts report neutral villages Huesca and Castellon within reach. We strike now to capture both, expanding our territory to five villages. Reinforcements are sent to Tarragona to prepare for the next push towards Zaragoza.
B.plano: Send all troops from Girona to Huesca and from Tarragona to Castellon to capture both villages. Send 1 archer from Barcelona to Tarragona as reinforcement. Build 1 spearman and 1 archer in Barcelona to prepare for the next wave of attacks. Keep 1 knight in Barcelona for defense. Next turn, send the newly built troops and the knight to Tarragona to prepare for the attack on Zaragoza.

A.depoimento: I am launching a coordinated strike on the neutral villages of Evora, Porto, and Salamanca to expand my territory. My archers take Evora, while my spearman and knights capture Porto and Salamanca. I am building more archers to replenish my forces.
A.plano: Capture Evora, Porto, and Salamanca to expand to 6 villages. Focus on building archers to replenish losses and grow the army. Next turn, push towards Faro and Badajoz.

B.depoimento: King B's armies move! Huesca's warriors march to conquer Zaragoza and Pamplona. Our smithies work day and night forging new weapons. The expansion of our kingdom begins now!
B.plano: This turn: send Huesca's troops to attack Zaragoza (1 archer, 1 knight) and Pamplona (2 spearman, 1 knight). Build troops in all villages as listed. Next turn, assess losses, reinforce Zaragoza, and plan the attack on Valencia using Castellon's growing force.

A.depoimento: My armies strike on all fronts this turn. Santarem's newly built spearmen and archers march on Badajoz, while Porto's spearman and knight charge Vigo. Lisboa sends reinforcements to Evora, and Coimbra marches to Salamanca to prepare for the next wave of conquest. We expand our territory from 6 to 8 villages, paving the way to 18.
A.plano: Capture Badajoz and Vigo this turn. Reinforce Evora with 2 spearman and 1 archer from Lisboa, and Salamanca with 7 archers from Coimbra. Next turn, attack Faro from Evora with 2 spearman and 2 archers (keep 1 archer home to avoid archer majority), and attack Madrid from Salamanca with archers. Build 3 spearman in Santarem, 2 spearman in Lisboa, 2 archers in Coimbra.

B.depoimento: We launched a double-pronged attack on Zaragoza from Tarragona and Huesca to secure our northern border and open the road to Madrid. Our marching army engaged the strong garrison at Pamplona, sacrificing troops to wear down the enemy defenses. Meanwhile, our villages worked diligently, producing knights and archers to swell our ranks.
B.plano: This turn: build troops in all villages as planned. Send Tarragona's archers and knight, and Huesca's spearmen and archer, to attack Zaragoza [17] to conquer it next turn. The army marching to Pamplona will fight; we accept the loss but it will weaken the garrison. Next turn, reinforce Zaragoza and plan the attack on Pamplona from the newly conquered Zaragoza.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies strike at the neutral territories of Badajoz and Madrid, securing two new villages for our kingdom. We also reinforce our western flanks at Evora and Porto, while our forges work tirelessly to produce spearmen and knights, strengthening our position for the march east.
A.plano: Conquer Badajoz from Santarem and Madrid from Salamanca this turn. Reinforce Evora with 2 spearman from Lisboa and Porto with 2 archers from Coimbra. Build 2 spearman in Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, Porto, Salamanca, and 1 knight in Coimbra to grow our army for next turn's expansions.

A.depoimento: We launched a double-pronged attack this turn, sending our elite forces from Evora to conquer the neutral village of Faro, while our Madrid garrison marches on Burgos to secure our northern border. Simultaneously, we are rushing reinforcements from Salamanca to Madrid to strengthen our defenses against any enemy counter-offensive from Zaragoza. Our villages are working at full capacity, producing a steady stream of spearman and knights to fuel our next wave of conquests.
A.plano: Conquer Faro from Evora and Burgos from Madrid this turn. Reinforce Madrid from Salamanca with all available troops to guard the border. Build 2 spearman in Lisboa, Santarem, Coimbra, Porto, Salamanca, Vigo, and 1 knight in Evora to grow our army for next turn's expansions towards Toledo and Zaragoza.

A.depoimento: This turn, we focus on securing our northern flank by attacking Pamplona from Burgos. We are sending reinforcements from Vigo and Madrid to Burgos, and from Salamanca to Madrid. We are also building archers and spearmen across our villages to prepare for the next push towards Zaragoza and Toledo.
A.plano: Focus on expanding north and east. Attack Pamplona from Burgos with archer and knight. Reinforce Burgos from Vigo and Madrid. Reinforce Madrid from Salamanca. Build archers and spearmen in all productive villages to grow the army for next turn's push towards Zaragoza and Toledo.

B.depoimento: This turn, I am attacking Pamplona with 2 spearmen and 1 archer from Zaragoza to capture it and expand my territory. I am also building spearmen in all my villages to strengthen my army for future battles.
B.plano: After capturing Pamplona, start building there to secure the new village. Check if Madrid attacks Zaragoza; if not, reinforce Zaragoza with new spearmen builds. Prepare for next attack on Madrid by gathering troops.

B.depoimento: Our forces are moving on all fronts. Pamplona will fall this turn, and Valencia is being assaulted. We are building up a giant army in Zaragoza to crush Madrid. The enemy cannot stop our expansion!
B.plano: Build 2 spearman in all villages. Send Castellon's force to Valencia. Send Tarragona and Huesca reinforcements to Zaragoza. Keep Zaragoza's garrison to defend and prepare for the Madrid attack next turn. Send Barcelona and Girona troops to Zaragoza to build up the main army.

A.depoimento: I am preparing a massive offensive from Badajoz to conquer the neutral villages of Toledo and Sevilha. I have built specialized troops: knights to break Toledo's archers and spearmen to defeat Sevilha's knights. I am concentrating my forces in Badajoz while reinforcing my border villages of Madrid and Burgos to secure my flanks.
A.plano: Build knights in Santarem and Salamanca to counter Toledo's archers. Build spearmen in Badajoz and Faro to counter Sevilha's knights. Send reinforcements to Badajoz to prepare for the double attack on Toledo and Sevilha next turn. Reinforce Madrid and Burgos with archers and troops from Salamanca and Vigo to defend against enemy counter-attacks.

B.depoimento: Our armies move on multiple fronts: the main force from Zaragoza marches on Madrid, Valencia's troops assault Murcia, and Huesca reinforces Pamplona. The eastern villages send their best to Zaragoza to prepare for the next push. We build archers and knights to complement our spearmen.
B.plano: Attack Madrid with Zaragoza's main army, leaving a small garrison. Reinforce Pamplona with Huesca's troops. Attack Murcia with Valencia's troops. Send reinforcements from eastern villages to Zaragoza. Build archers and knights. Next turn, check Madrid and explore west.

A.depoimento: I have launched a coordinated attack on the neutral villages of Toledo and Sevilha to expand my territory. Archers from Badajoz and Madrid will assault Toledo, while spearmen from Badajoz and Faro will attack Sevilha. I am reinforcing Madrid with knights from Salamanca to secure my border against counter-attacks. Across my kingdom, I am building new troops to replenish losses and maintain momentum. Capturing these villages will bring me closer to my goal of 18 villages.
A.plano: Focus on capturing neutral villages Toledo and Sevilha to expand to 13 villages. Badajoz sends archers to Toledo and spearmen to Sevilha; Madrid sends archers to Toledo as a second wave; Faro sends spearmen to Sevilha. Salamanca reinforces Madrid with knights. Building troops across the realm to replenish losses and prepare for further expansion. Watch enemy reinforcements to Zaragoza and Pamplona; consider attacking Pamplona next turn if its garrison remains weak. Do not engage Zaragoza yet.

B.depoimento: My archers lead the assault on Madrid, their numbers triggering the counter bonus against the enemy spearman. Reinforcements stream east to west, feeding the next offensive while Zaragoza holds a reserve of 13 spearman. The freshly taken Murcia grows stronger with Valencia's troops. This is the turn I break the enemy's western wall.
B.plano: Attack Madrid from Zaragoza with 3 spearman, 4 archer, 2 knight — archer is most numerous, triggering 1.5x counter bonus against their spearman (effective attack ~28 vs defense 15). Keep 13 spearman in Zaragoza for defense and next offensive. Build 2 archers in Zaragoza for next turn. Tarragona and Huesca send reinforcements to Zaragoza. Valencia's 5 spearman reinforce Murcia. Castellon sends 2 spearman to Valencia. After Madrid falls, attack Salamanca or Toledo from Madrid.

A.depoimento: Turn 12: The grand assault begins! My spearmen storm Sevilha, archers rake Cordoba and Madrid. I am building knights in every capable village to forge a swift, deadly core. Reinforcements pour to the borders: Vigo's spearman brace Burgos, while archers from the interior flood Salamanca. The enemy capital waits, but I will take these three villages first, then push deeper. Onward to 18!
A.plano: Turn 12: Three-pronged offensive. Sevilha: 15 spearmen arrive. Cordoba: Toledo archers assault, Badajoz archers follow. Madrid: Burgos and Salamanca archers attack. Reinforce Burgos (Vigo spearman) and Salamanca (Porto, Coimbra, Lisboa archers). Build knights everywhere. Send Evora/Santarem to Badajoz as reserve. Next turn: capture all three, then target Teruel/Pamplona. Avoid Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: King B's forces launch a double attack on Salamanca and Cordoba. The Madrid garrison leads the assault on Salamanca, with a Zaragoza strike force following. Murcia's army captures Cordoba. We reinforce Madrid and Pamplona against expected enemy counterattacks, while building archers and knights across the realm.
B.plano: Salamanca attacked by Madrid (turn 13) and Zaragoza (turn 14). Cordoba attacked by Murcia (turn 13). Madrid reinforced by Zaragoza, Barcelona, Castellon (turn 13) and Tarragona (turn 14). Pamplona reinforced by Huesca (turn 13) and Girona (turn 14). Build archers and knights. Next turn: reinforce Salamanca and Cordoba, explore west, attack Toledo from Madrid.

A.depoimento: I am launching a decisive offensive against the enemy's weakest points. Madrid and Murcia are poorly defended, and I will capture them to bring my total to 15 villages. My archers from Salamanca and spearmen from Burgos will overwhelm Madrid's garrison, while Cordoba's archers strike Murcia. I am also reinforcing my borders to prepare for the enemy's inevitable counter-attacks. The time to expand is now!
A.plano: Focus on capturing Madrid and Murcia. Madrid is weakly defended (1 knight) and Murcia has only 1 archer. I am sending all available archers from Salamanca and spearmen/knights from Burgos to take Madrid. Cordoba's archers will take Murcia. I am reinforcing Sevilha's troops to Cordoba for the next push. I am also sending knights from my interior villages to the borders (Salamanca, Burgos, Badajoz) to defend against enemy counter-attacks. Building knights and archers everywhere to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: I am launching a double offensive on the eastern front. My elite troops from Madrid are marching on Zaragoza, while Cordoba's spearman reinforce Murcia for the push on Valencia. I am also strengthening my interior defenses by moving troops from Badajoz to Salamanca and from Vigo to Burgos. The noose is tightening on King B.
A.plano: Focus on capturing Zaragoza and Valencia. Zaragoza is weakly defended (20) and I am sending a strong army from Madrid. Valencia is also weak (13) and I am reinforcing Murcia from Cordoba to attack it next turn. I am reinforcing Madrid from Salamanca and Salamanca from Badajoz to maintain a strong defense. I am also reinforcing Burgos from Vigo. I am building troops in Murcia, Cordoba, Salamanca, Burgos, and Toledo to maintain momentum. I must watch out for enemy counter-attacks on Murcia.

B.depoimento: My armies strike on all fronts this turn! Valencia takes Murcia, Pamplona takes Burgos, and Castellon's knights capture Teruel. I am building up my forces across the realm, preparing for the push into the western lands. The enemy will not stop our expansion!
B.plano: We are attacking Murcia, Burgos, and Teruel this turn. We must ensure we send 3 spearman and 5 archers to Burgos to avoid the counter triangle and secure victory. Castellon's 3 knights will take Teruel. Zaragoza sends 4 spearman to reinforce Pamplona. We build knights in Barcelona and Castellon, and archers everywhere else.

A.depoimento: I ordered the assault on Burgos and Valencia, sending my full strength from Madrid and Murcia. Vigo sends knights as a second wave. I am reinforcing Madrid and Murcia for next turn. My armies should easily overcome the weak enemy defenses.
A.plano: Attack Burgos from Madrid and Valencia from Murcia to conquer two villages. Reinforce Madrid with Salamanca and Toledo, and Murcia with Cordoba. Build troops in all villages for future offensives. Next turn, attack Teruel from Valencia to reach 18 villages. Must defend Zaragoza from Pamplona. Do not attack Pamplona yet.

B.depoimento: The western frontier opens with barely a struggle — Vigo's empty fields fall to a handful of spears. Every forge from Barcelona to Pamplona burns bright as knights and archers pour from the workshops. We are building the army that will shatter Madrid's walls and march to Lisboa itself.
B.plano: Send 2 spearman from Burgos to Vigo (defense 0, trivial win). Build 1 knight in Barcelona, Castellon, Valencia, and Burgos; 2 archers in Tarragona, Girona, Huesca, and Pamplona. Castellon needs 1 more knight to field 3 for Teruel next turn (3 knights with counter = 18 > 13). Keep 2 archer at Burgos for defense against Madrid. 4 spearmen arrive at Pamplona next turn from Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: We bolster our eastern defenses by shifting knights to Tarragona and archers to Castellon, while our knights leap to attack Teruel. The enemy will find us stronger and our reach expanding.
B.plano: Move 2 knights from Barcelona to Tarragona, 3 archers from Tarragona to Castellon, and 3 knights from Castellon to Teruel. Build 1 knight in Barcelona and Pamplona; 1 archer in Tarragona, Girona, Castellon, and Huesca.

A.depoimento: I am launching a decisive attack on Teruel from Zaragoza to claim my 18th village. At the same time, I am reinforcing my northern and eastern borders to prepare for any enemy counteroffensive. My economy is thriving, and I am converting resources into a massive army.
A.plano: Capture Teruel to reach 18 villages and secure the win condition. Reinforce Valencia, Burgos, and Toledo to defend the borders. Build troops in all major villages to maintain economic and military growth.

B.depoimento: I launch a two-pronged offensive: my knights from Teruel sweep into Toledo, while Pamplona's full might storms Burgos. I reinforce Castellon with archers from Tarragona to hold the southern front. All villages build archers and knights to feed the war machine.
B.plano: Attack Toledo from Teruel with 2 knights (defense 3, easy win). Attack Burgos from Pamplona with all 16 troops (9 spearman, 5 archer, 2 knight) — attack 27 vs defense 18. Reinforce Castellon with 4 archers from Tarragona to shore up its weak defense. Build 1 knight in Barcelona and Pamplona, 2 archers everywhere else. Accept risk that Pamplona and Teruel are left exposed.

A.depoimento: My armies march on Teruel to secure the 18th village and trigger the win condition. I am reinforcing my borders heavily with knights from Madrid, Murcia, Badajoz, and Cordoba to ensure the enemy cannot push back. All villages are building troops at maximum capacity to dominate the battlefield.
A.plano: Capture Teruel with the marching army to reach 18 villages. Reinforce Zaragoza, Valencia, Toledo, and Burgos to secure borders and prepare for holding the newly expanded territory. Build troops in all villages to maintain economic and military growth.

B.depoimento: The arrows fly at Zaragoza this turn — nine archers from Huesca with the counter bonus against their spearmen should carry the city. Meanwhile, I rush six archers from Castellon to shore up Teruel's empty walls before the enemy host arrives. Barcelona's knights ride to Tarragona as a reserve. If Zaragoza falls, the road to Madrid opens; if Teruel holds, my southern flank stands firm.
B.plano: Attack Zaragoza with all 9 archers from Huesca — archer counters spearmen (defender's majority), effective attack 27 vs defense 20. Reinforce Teruel with 6 archers from Castellon before the enemy army arrives. Send Barcelona's 3 knights to Tarragona to thicken the border defense. Build spearmen everywhere to prepare for Toledo (enemy knights) and general defense. Watch Castellon — it will be thin after sending troops away.

B.depoimento: Zaragoza slipped through my fingers last turn, but the enemy left only 2 knights to hold it. I march from Tarragona with 7 knights and 2 archers — 32 attack against a defense of 5. The road to Madrid will open again. Across my realm, every border village fires its forges: spearmen pour out, cheap and deadly against the enemy's knights. I will not lose ground while I strike.
B.plano: Attack Zaragoza with all Tarragona troops — 7 knights lead, overwhelming the 2-knight garrison. Build 2 spearmen in every border village (Barcelona, Castellon, Huesca, Teruel, Pamplona) plus 2 archers in Girona and 1 archer in Tarragona. After Zaragoza falls, Tarragona becomes interior and I can march on Madrid. Watch Castellon and Teruel for enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: I have launched a double offensive on the enemy's western flank, sending the full garrisons of Burgos and Valencia to take Pamplona and Castellon. If both attacks succeed, I will finally reach the 18-village threshold needed to win. Meanwhile, my villages are producing knights at maximum capacity to secure the new borders and prepare for the next push towards the enemy capital.
A.plano: Conquer Pamplona [19] from Burgos [14] and Castellon [18] from Valencia [16] this turn to reach 18 villages. Build knights in all border villages (Toledo, Madrid, Burgos, Valencia) and interior villages to prepare for defending the new borders and launching further attacks on Teruel and Zaragoza next turn. Do not attack Zaragoza yet; wait for Madrid to build up more knights.

B.depoimento: We launched an attack on Madrid with our knights and archers from Zaragoza. We reinforced Zaragoza with archers from Girona and a knight from Barcelona, while also strengthening Pamplona with spearman from Huesca and Castellon with an archer from Tarragona. We built new spearman and archers in our villages to grow our army for the next push.
B.plano: Check the battle report for Madrid. If victorious, move troops from Zaragoza to Madrid to garrison it. Then decide next attack: Toledo (via Teruel) or Burgos (via Pamplona). Continue building troops. Watch for enemy counterattacks on our border villages.

A.depoimento: I am one village short of the 75% needed to win, and Huesca is the softest target on the board. I am sending a fast archer-and-knight strike from Pamplona to take it this turn, while my border villages build up their garrisons for whatever King B throws back next.
A.plano: Target Huesca [20] (defense 5, weakest visible enemy) from Pamplona [19] with 6 archer + 3 knight, arriving in 1 turn; archers counter its spearmen for 1.5x damage. Keep 2 spearmen at Pamplona as garrison. Rebuild at Pamplona, Valencia, Castellon, Burgos, Toledo, Salamanca. Need just 1 more village to hold 18/24 for the win.

A.depoimento: We are strengthening our borders and attacking Tarragona to secure our hold on the map. Victory is within reach if we defend well.
A.plano: We must hold 18 villages this turn to get the consecutive win. Pamplona is weak, but we build there and send reinforcements from Huesca and Vigo to Burgos. We attack Tarragona to ensure we have a backup village if Pamplona falls. Build spearmen in all border villages to boost defense.

B.depoimento: I have ordered my knights to strike at Pamplona, a weak point in the enemy's defenses. Meanwhile, I am strengthening my borders and building up my forces for the campaigns to come. The war for dominance continues.
B.plano: Attack Pamplona with 3 knights from Zaragoza. Send 2 spearman from Barcelona to Girona for defense. Build troops as listed. Next turn, if Pamplona falls, send reinforcements from Zaragoza. Prepare Girona to attack Huesca with knights. Prepare Tarragona to attack Castellon with archers.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched a two-pronged assault on Madrid from Salamanca and Toledo, and struck Zaragoza from Huesca. We also sent waves of reinforcements from our interior villages to the border, and built up our garrisons. Our goal is to secure our hold on 18 villages and expand into enemy territory.
A.plano: We launched offensives on Madrid from Salamanca and Toledo, and on Zaragoza from Huesca, aiming to capture these enemy villages and reduce threats. We sent reinforcements from interior villages to Salamanca, Toledo, Burgos, and Valencia to rebuild border garrisons. We built troops in all villages. If we captured Madrid and Zaragoza, we should have at least 18 villages. Next turn, reinforce new territories and continue building. Watch for enemy counterattacks.
